title: Insurance Photo Coverage Completeness
dataSources: Collection items (`collection:item`), intake scans (`collection:scan`), market prices (`collection:price`), item photos (`collection:photo`), authentication records (`collection:auth`), loans (`collection:loan`), and condition audits (`collection:condition`).
app: Collection telemetry from personal catalogues, NFC scans, pricing feeds, authentication records, loan logs, shelf measurements, and item-condition audits streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=collection:photo
| stats sum(eval(if(photo_count>0,1,0))) as covered_items count as total_items by collection_type
| eval coverage_pct=round(100*covered_items/total_items,1)
description: Measures what share of items in each collection has at least one insurance-ready photo on file.
value: Photo coverage matters when claims or valuations arise, and it is far easier to improve when the gaps are obvious.
implementation: Track the number of reference photos for each item as part of your catalogue or inventory workflow.
visualization: Bar chart of photo-coverage percentage by collection type.
grandmaExplanation: It warns how much of your collection has good photos on file in case you ever need proof for insurance.
